Inherited from dc_qp: on stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (by reading; age 80, dc_incapable yes, a qualifying person under p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "In determining whether a person is a qualifying person, a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025") the project checks column (c) and the candidate, whose dc_qp needs months > 6, does not; i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled". It also omits f2441.care, so it checks the box on a return with no care (the Claude class M case classm.dependent.1 dep_b). Representation: for a 13-year-old, "dc_under13 no" implies all included care was at 13 or older, which is the project's dc_over12_care yes on consistent answers.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error with the prior presentation ambiguity retained; i2441 (2025) pp.3-4 Column(d) excludes benefits for the person listed, but the reply subtracts the entire form-level line28 from every dependent entry. A household total is not a per-person allocation: with two people each having $1,000 expenses and $1,000 total excluded benefits, applying that same subtraction to both rows removes $2,000. The current interface supplies gross entry expenses and adjusts benefits once at form level. The existing gross-column/net-line30 choice amb.2025.dc_line30 remains recorded; this ruling makes no new owner decision or claim of per-row allocation support.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on admitted facts; i1040gi (2025) pp.17-19 Steps1-5 give the dependency and credit prerequisites. The child citizenship, dependent TIN/work-SSN and household.ctc_ssn conditions match. Its joint-return/claimable-filer alternative extends an excluded sa.dependent=true regime; no equivalence or admission of that regime is claimed. This ruling is limited to the qualifying-child credit results, not the separate QR/care outputs.

The project supplies Count1 and filters at f2441.qp_count; the second supplies Count1 conditionally. This adjudicates only placement of the count filter, not correctness of the second qualifying-person predicate, whose defects are ruled separately. No whole-tree equivalence or standalone nonqualifier value is claimed.

The candidate's disabled route is "dc_incapable and months > 6", with no death-year rule, though dependent.born_died and dependent.part_year_home were published (BUG-0157 added dependent.dc_lived_half after round 2, so round 2's scope ruling no longer covers the line): p503 p. 3, Birth or death of otherwise qualifying person: "In determining whether a person is a qualifying person, a person who was born or died in 2025 is treated as having lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your home was the person's home more than half the time they were alive in 2025". Witness by reading (not executed): regression stage15.f2441.parent_died_part_year (BUG-0157): a disabled parent, age 80, who died in 2025, months 0 as the months question instructs for a non-qualifying-child person not with you the entire time, born_died yes, part_year_home yes, dc_incapable yes, dc_paid $4,000; the project gives dc_qp yes (dependent.dc_lived_half), 2(d) $4,000 and f2441 line 11 $600; the candidate's disabled route needs months > 6 and gives dc_qp no. Other differences: (a) its route for a disabled person who would be a dependent except for gross income or a joint return is behind the project's cited screen f2441.nondependent (i2441 p. 1, "or could claim as a dependent except"), scope; (b) it omits f2441.care, which reaches no amount (Form 2441 sums only where dc_qp holds and is not completed without care); (c) sa.dependent omission is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead); (d) its sibling_descendant variant is the odc_person error.

The corrected reply tests claimed, residence and age but does not require qualifying-child status, so an unrelated all-year QR child can be treated as a care qualifying person without incapacity. The reply now derives the age regimes without requiring an unnecessary dc_under13 answer and matches all ten declared qualifying-person outputs. It additionally encodes disabled would-be dependents that this project refuses through f2441.nondependent; no admission or equivalence of that excluded regime is claimed. The missing care-screen factor is irrelevant on the active care rows compared here. Its separate column(c) contract failure remains blocking.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: collection parent binding mismatch), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. (1) The candidate requires months > 6 for every Test 2 person, with no part-year route for a relative other than a qualifying child born, dying, adopted or placed in 2025, though dependent.born_died, dependent.placed and dependent.part_year_home were published: i1040gi p. 15: "If the person is your qualifying child, the child must have lived with you for more than half the part of the year the child was alive. If the person is anyone else, see Pub. 501. Similarly, if you adopted the person ... the person is considered to have lived with you for more than half of 2025 if your main home was this person's main home for more than half the time since the person was adopted or placed with you in 2025"; p501 p. 9, Death or birth: "Your qualifying child or qualifying relative who lived with you for more than half the part of the year they were alive". Witness by reading (not executed): regression stage8.hoh.adopted_part_year (BUG-0158): an adult child adopted in 2025, a qualifying relative with months 0 and part_year_home yes, placed yes; the project gives hoh_test2 yes (line 12e $23,625 head of household), the candidate gives no because it needs months > 6; the stage8 death-year parent case (born_died yes, part_year_home yes) is the same. (2) Its dependent test counts a sibling_descendant qualifying relative who did not live with you all year: i1040gi p. 19, Step 4: a qualifying relative is your "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" or "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household" (a grandniece or a stepsibling's child, the project's sibling_descendant, is not in the relationship list); such a person is not your dependent, so Test 2 (i1040gi p. 14, item 1(b)) cannot use them. Round 2 ruled the same two errors. sa.dependent omission is scope (the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead).

This affects the transitive dependency of this line. The raw response is preserved, not silently repaired. BUG-0129 records that the comparer erases the annotation; .transcription/constant-unit-erasure-witness.json confirms the false-agreement mechanism. This is a model IR error, not a project tax-value finding. The separate transcription qualification hold remains in force.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on admitted eligible-TIN facts; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Steps4-5 requires the same QR income/support/residency/all-year relationship conditions and ODC citizenship/household identification conditions. The reply places dependent.tin inside claimed instead of as a separate ODC factor; both are true on admitted identified dependents. Its MFJ/claimable-filer branch extends a refused regime, and lack-of-dependent-TIN refusal placement differs; neither excluded regime is admitted by this ruling. The separate HOH and care-box defects remain pending.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 and Step5 require the all-year household route for otherwise eligible other/sibling_descendant relationships and identification for both filers when jointly filing. The corrected reply QR helper excludes those relationships outright and its ODC predicate omits household.all_tin. An eligible all-year distant relative can be wrongly rejected, and the filer-TIN prerequisite is not encoded. Invalid dc_count is a separate form-level failure, not a reason to treat these source omissions as equivalence.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the returned h_qr_relationship treats sibling_descendant as an unconditional listed Step4 relative and omits other even with twelve household months. The published input defines sibling_descendant as more distant descendants (for example grandnieces and a stepsibling child); listed nieces/nephews are already in sibling. i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 requires the all-year household condition for these other relationships; p501 p.19 excludes foster parents from listed parents. On the saved seven-month distant-relative case the project gives ODC false/$0, the actual model gives true/$500; an all-year other household member reverses that error. The actual-expression witness is .transcription/dependent-age-claude-witness.json. Untyped Count constants are an additional model IR defect (BUG-0129), not an excuse to call the trees equivalent.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on admitted eligible-TIN facts; i1040gi (2025) p.19 Steps4-5 requires the same QR income/support/residency/all-year relationship conditions and ODC citizenship/household identification conditions. The reply places dependent.tin inside claimed instead of as a separate ODC factor; both are true on admitted identified dependents. Its MFJ/claimable-filer branch extends a refused regime, and lack-of-dependent-TIN refusal placement differs; neither excluded regime is admitted by this ruling. The separate HOH and care-box defects remain pending.

The corrected reply QR helper excludes those relationships outright and its ODC predicate omits household.all_tin. An eligible all-year distant relative can be wrongly rejected, and the filer-TIN prerequisite is not encoded. Invalid dc_count is a separate form-level failure, not a reason to treat these source omissions as equivalence.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi (2025) pp.18-19 Steps3-5 distinguish the residency/citizenship and filer identification requirements for the credits. The reply omits the ODC citizenship and household.all_tin tests, and its QR relationship helper omits sibling_descendant even when the person meets the all-year household condition. The published enum reserves that category for more distant relatives; a lawful all-year eligible person may qualify under Step4. These are source/interface omissions, not equivalence or new owner scope choices.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; Not executable: the reply fails validation (dependent.dc_count: collection parent binding mismatch), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/dependent.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line is outside that error's dependency closure and is ruled by reading the expressions against the source. (1) The candidate omits the filer SSN-or-ITIN test (household.all_tin: every person has a TIN or applied for an ITIN): i1040gi p. 19, Step 5: "1. Did you, and your spouse if filing a joint return, have either an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)? ... No. STOP You can't claim the credit for other dependents"; p. 17, Before you begin: "If you want to claim the credit for other dependents, you, and your spouse if filing jointly, must have either an SSN or ITIN"; a filer with no SSN or ITIN gets $500 per other dependent where the source gives none. (2) Its qualifying-relative route treats sibling_descendant as a relative who need not live with you all year: i1040gi p. 19, Step 4: a qualifying relative is your "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" or "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household" (a grandniece or a stepsibling's child, the project's sibling_descendant, is not in the relationship list). (3) Omitting sa.dependent (listed as a refusal gate) is scope: the project refuses every return with sa.dependent yes: sa.standard, a Schedule A line evaluated on every return, refuses on sa.dependent ("Dependent and dual-status standard deductions are outside this resident nondependent slice", i1040gi pp. 34-35, line 12e), so no computed return reaches the difference ; the candidate lists sa.dependent among its refusal gates instead. (4) Its added "dependent.joint_return is no" on the qualifying-relative route is representation, because dependent.qualifying_relative refuses on dependent.married (i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, question 3, "See Married person").

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the returned h_qr_relationship treats sibling_descendant as an unconditional listed Step4 relative and omits other even with twelve household months. The published input defines sibling_descendant as more distant descendants (for example grandnieces and a stepsibling child); listed nieces/nephews are already in sibling. i1040gi (2025) p.19 Step4 requires the all-year household condition for these other relationships; p501 p.19 excludes foster parents from listed parents. On the saved seven-month distant-relative case the project gives ODC false/$0, the actual model gives true/$500; an all-year other household member reverses that error. The actual-expression witness is .transcription/dependent-age-claude-witness.json. Untyped Count constants are an additional model IR defect (BUG-0129), not an excuse to call the trees equivalent.
